purpose: Semantic Correctness Oracle. Expected fields are written by hand from the raw line and the cited specification text, never copied from a parser run. resolvedDefects.F-1: RFC 3164 line without HOSTNAME lost its first key=value field into the header in both executors. Resolved by BSD_HOSTNAME and the rfc3164_hostless rule of contracts/syslog-header-grammar.v1.json.
resolvedDefects.F-2: RFC 5424 VERSION policy differed between consumers. Resolved by semantics.rfc5424SupportedVersions, read by every consumer.
resolvedDefects.F-3: U+2028 inside a value was rejected by the browser and parsed by the generated Ruby. Resolved by the portable token REST = [^\r\n]+.
resolvedDefects.F-4: RFC 5424 TIMESTAMP with an impossible calendar day was rejected by the browser and parsed by the generated Ruby. Resolved by an explicit calendar check beside Time.iso8601 in both Ruby templates.
resolvedDefects.F-5: A TAG directly after the timestamp ('kernel:', 'sshd[123]:') was read as HOSTNAME by both executors when HOSTNAME was omitted. Resolved by BSD_HOSTNAME not ending in ':'; the line is declined.
resolvedDefects.F-6: The Python Multi-Pass fallback parsed an RFC 5424 line with VERSION 999. Resolved by semantics.rfc5424SupportedVersions and the rfc5424_version_head fragment, read by every Python entry point.
resolvedDefects.F-7: The strict key=value path of the browser and the generated Ruby accepted U+001C..U+001F as value data while Generic Structural and the Python preview declined the line (issue #214). Resolved by KV_BARE excluding U+001C..U+001F.
resolvedDefects.F-8: The Python Multi-Pass key=value scanner split pairs at Unicode white space (NBSP, U+2028) and decoded a different escape set than the browser and Ruby. Resolved by the scanner reading fragments.kv_pair and semantics.kvUnescapedAfterBackslash.
resolvedDefects.F-9: A CEF or LEEF line with U+2028 inside a value was rejected by the browser ('.' excludes it in ECMAScript) and parsed by the generated Ruby and the Python preview. Resolved by dotAll on the two family head expressions.
resolvedDefects.F-10: The Python preview reported a line that claims to be CEF or LEEF but is not valid (six header fields, LEEF 3.0) as parsed through its permissive Generic Structural fallback, with multi-word values cut at the first space. Resolved for the Python preview by fragments.structured_family_claim. The browser and Ruby side is policy divergence D-2.
resolvedDefects.F-11: CEF and LEEF: the header splitter also decoded backslash escapes in the extension, which the extension grammar then decoded a second time, identically in the browser and the generated Ruby. 'filePath=C:\\\\Users\\\\new' came out as 'C:\\Users' LF 'ew', and the standard's own example 'act=blocked a \\\\ dst=1.1.1.1' lost dst. Resolved by keeping the text after the last header delimiter exactly as written.
resolvedDefects.F-12: The Python preview offered a comma row with a double quote inside a bare field (aaa,b\"bb,ccc) as a CSV candidate; RFC 4180 forbids it and the browser tokenizer and Ruby's CSV.parse_line reject the row. Resolved in parse_csv_spans.
resolvedDefects.F-13: The Python preview parsed a CEF:1 line while the browser and the generated Ruby implement CEF version 0 only, so the Analyze step showed a line as parsed that the generated parser rejects. Resolved by semantics.cefSupportedVersions, read by every engine.

D-1.statement: A field written more than once in one event is never resolved by keeping one of its values. The Python source preview keeps the original key and every value in wire order and does not report the event as completely parsed (issue DUPLICATE_SOURCE_FIELD). The browser extractor and the generated Ruby decline the event; the browser names the repeated field and the reason. While a repeated field is unresolved no engine reports FULL.
enforcedBy: cases with expect.repeated (hand-written and model-rendered key=value bodies)

D-2.statement: A line that starts with CEF: or LEEF: handed to Generic Structural WITHOUT a selected profile: the browser and the generated Ruby still parse it with the legacy space-separated key=value route, which leaves the header and the first attribute as unparsed text (kept deliberately for existing V15 projects: src/guided/leef2ProfilePrecedence20261020.test.ts, backend/test/leef2-profile-precedence.test.ts, backend/test/generic-structural-mixed-profile-v1.test.ts). The Python preview declines such a line when it is not valid CEF/LEEF. Declining it in the browser and Ruby as well changes the output of existing projects and needs an owner decision.
